newsitem.title: UK: European bonds cheer EMU progress but mark nervous.
newsitem.headline: European bonds cheer EMU progress but mark nervous.

text.p: European bond markets were riding high on Monday, optimistic about a potential deal to unblock a single European currency logjam, but any accord could spell trouble for the mark, analysts said.

"The markets are hopeful for a deal," said Sonja Gibbs, senior bond strategist at Nomura International in London. "There is so much pressure on these leaders to get a deal done that I'm sure they can come up with something."

A deal would hurt the mark, sparking expectations that Europe's linchpin currency would be traded in for a weaker euro if heavy public borrowers like Italy joined Europe's economic and monetary union at the launch in 1999, traders said.
But that prospect set a positive spin on bonds with peripheral markets looking poised for more gains if criteria were fudged, traders said.
Whatever the market fallout, analysts are fairly sure some agreement will be reached.
Huw Roberts, European bond strategist at NatWest Capital Markets, said, "At the end of the day there is so much political capital that has been invested in it that...politicians will win through."

European finance ministers, in Amsterdam for a two-day European Union summit starting on Monday, said repeatedly after weekend meetings they were close to agreement, although no details were unveiled on what form this would be.

The sticky issue of the stability pact has caused a stalemate in the European agenda after French demands to attach a protocol on employment to the pact's complex rules designed to ensure budget discipline after the euro is launched.
In European morning trade, the mark had pared losses it incurred against the dollar last week in anticipation of a deal,
